sources.title: Léopold Sédar Senghor, Chants d'ombre (1945) and Hosties noires (1948) — his own poetry collections, the latter written substantially from his WWII POW experience
Senghor's own Négritude essays, co-developed with Aimé Césaire and Léon Damas in 1930s Paris
Janet Vaillant, Black, French, and African: A Life of Léopold Sédar Senghor (1990)

autonomy_need.rationale: Voluntarily resigned Senegal's presidency in 1980 after twenty years in office — one of very few African heads of state of his generation to leave power voluntarily rather than through coup, death, or force, and a specific, dated, well-documented act.

creative_originality.rationale: Co-founded the Négritude literary and philosophical movement with Aimé Césaire and Léon Damas in 1930s Paris, a specific, documented original intellectual contribution with lasting influence on later African and diaspora thought.

persistence.rationale: Continued writing poetry through nearly two years as a German POW (1940-1942) after his capture serving in the French army — a specific, dated episode of sustained creative output under real, documented hardship.

discipline.rationale: Maintained continuous literary output — including work composed during POW captivity — alongside two decades of active state leadership, a documented sustained dual practice, not a single productive period.

collaboration.rationale: Sustained a documented, decades-long intellectual partnership with Aimé Césaire in developing Négritude, evidenced by their extensive surviving correspondence and co-published work.

leadership_drive.rationale: Served as Senegal's first president for twenty years (1960-1980), a documented sustained leadership role, though the voluntary-resignation pattern (autonomy_need) suggests power was not held as an end in itself.

impact_motivation.rationale: Sustained a consistent, documented dual commitment across his life to African cultural affirmation and to Senegalese nation-building, without the major personal-enrichment scandals documented for some contemporaries.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Functioned at a verifiably high level in two genuinely distinct domains — internationally recognized poetry (culminating in his 1983 election as the first African member of the Académie française) and two decades as an active head of state.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Sustained decades of serious poetic output recognized at the highest institutional level available to a Francophone writer — his 1983 election to the Académie française is a specific, documented mark of sustained mastery, not a general reputation.

adaptability.rationale: Moved through documented, distinct life phases — POW captivity, colonial-era French legislator, head of a newly independent state, and elder statesman/academician — across one unusually eventful life.

independent_thinking.rationale: Négritude was a genuinely original intellectual departure at the time — asserting African cultural identity and values on their own terms rather than through inherited European frameworks — a documented, specific theoretical contribution.

ambiguity_tolerance.rationale: Sustained the genuinely difficult, often criticized balance of maintaining close diplomatic and economic ties with France while championing African cultural independence across two decades in office — a real, sustained tension, not a resolved position.

proactive_agency.rationale: Both the founding of Négritude and the 1980 resignation were self-initiated decisions, not actions forced by external circumstance in the moment.

planning_orientation.rationale: Executed an orderly, planned 1980 transfer of power to his chosen successor Abdou Diouf rather than a chaotic exit — a specific, documented act of succession planning.

achievement_drive.rationale: Sustained pursuit of recognition in two demanding domains simultaneously across decades, evidenced by the range of documented achievement (the presidency, the Académie française) rather than a single stated ambition.

curiosity.rationale: Broad intellectual engagement across poetry, cultural theory, and governance is documented by the range of his output, though inferred from that breadth rather than a directly stated account of curiosity.

persuasiveness.rationale: Négritude's documented lasting influence on later Pan-African and diaspora intellectual movements suggests real persuasive reach, inferred from that reception rather than a single persuasive episode.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Chose to return to lead a newly independent Senegal in 1960 with genuinely uncertain prospects, rather than remain in his already-established literary career in France — inferred from that choice rather than a directly documented statement of risk acceptance.

provenance.notes: Roster-12 new-intake batch (2026-09): Sub-Saharan Africa pick. The 1980 voluntary resignation is treated as the strongest single piece of evidence in the pack — genuinely rare among his contemporaries and independently corroborated by the historical record of the transition itself, not just his own account. The France/Africa balance is scored honestly as dual_edged (ambiguity_tolerance) rather than resolved in his favor, since it was a real, contested tension in his own record. Scored to completion before any eligibility check was run.
